0.title: Introduction
0.transcript:
Every conversation you have as a Zydus sales professional carries the weight of a 74-year legacy.  

Zydus was built by Mr. Ramanbhai B. Patel, a first-generation entrepreneur with a simple conviction: that healthcare should reach the people who need it most. That conviction has grown into a global healthcare business spanning formulations, biologics, vaccines and wellness products, which reach patients across continents. 

You are now part of that story. But a legacy this size is only as strong as the person standing in front of a doctor, pharmacist or hospital administrator today. When you walk into a clinic or a chemist’s counter, you are not simply selling a product. You represent a brand, a set of values and a promise made to patients you will never meet. 

This course will introduce you to the fundamentals of that role. You will learn how to carry yourself as a representative of the organisation, how to build genuine engagement with healthcare customers, how to talk about product value in a way that is clear and credible and how to maintain the professional standards that protect both you and the organisation you represent. 

By the end of this course, you should be able to: 

  • Describe the standards of conduct expected when representing the organisation in front of healthcare customers 

  • Apply techniques for engaging healthcare customers professionally and building credible relationships 

  • Communicate product value clearly and compliantly during customer interactions

0.title: Applying Techniques for Engaging Healthcare Customers
0.header: Applying Techniques for Engaging Healthcare Customers
0.transcript:
Engaging a healthcare customer well means listening more than you speak. Doctors and pharmacists are pressed for time, so the representatives who stand out are the ones who ask thoughtful questions and genuinely register the answers. Sales trainer and author Neil Rackham’s research on high-performing sales conversations found that top performers spend more time understanding a customer’s specific needs before ever mentioning a product. Building credibility is less about what you say in the first minute, and more about what you notice. 

Let’s understand this with a scenario. 

Sarah, a sales professional, is meeting Dr. Coleman for the first time. Instead of opening with her product line, she asks what conditions he sees most often in his practice and what challenges his patients typically face with their current treatment plans. Dr. Coleman mentions that several of his patients struggle to remember complex dosing schedules. 

Sarah makes a note of this. In her next visit, she brings information specifically addressing dosing simplicity, tailored to what he told her. 

Dr. Coleman notices that she remembered, and he begins to see her as someone worth being available for, rather than another rep with a script. 

Sarah succeeded because she treated the conversation as a two-way exchange, not a pitch. Professional engagement with healthcare customers means asking thoughtful questions, listening closely and following up on what you learn. Credibility is built over time by showing that you pay attention.

0.title: Communicating Product Value Clearly and Compliantly During Customer Interactions
0.header: Communicating Product Value Clearly and Compliantly During Customer Interactions
0.transcript:
Communicating product value is not about listing every feature; it is about connecting a product’s benefits to a specific need the healthcare professional has already raised, within the bounds of what can be claimed. Regulatory bodies require ‘fair balance’ in promotional communication, meaning benefits must always be presented alongside relevant safety information, never in isolation. Getting this right protects the patient, the healthcare professional’s trust and the organisation’s licence to operate. 

Let’s understand this with a scenario. 

Kyle, a sales professional, is presenting a product to Dr. Whitfield. He leads with the dosing convenience, describing it as a solution that ‘works for virtually every patient’ and moves on to the next product before Dr. Whitfield can ask a follow-up question. He does not mention contraindications or reference the prescribing information. 

Later that week, Tom, another sales professional, presents the same product. He links the dosing convenience directly to a concern Dr. Whitfield raised earlier about patient adherence, then proactively covers the relevant safety information and contraindications, referencing the approved prescribing information rather than paraphrasing from memory. 

Dr. Whitfield tells his staff he is cautious about Kyle’s claims going forward, but he trusts Tom’s recommendations because Tom presents the full picture, not just the highlights. 

Compliant communication is not a constraint on selling well; it is what makes a sales conversation credible in the first place. Value that is not balanced with accurate safety information is not value at all; it is a liability waiting to surface.

0.title: Summary
0.transcript:
Congratulations!  

You have completed the course: Zydus Sales – Introduction Training 

In this course, you learnt that: 

  • Professional conduct, from punctuality to managing confidential information, builds the credibility that earns you continued access to healthcare customers 

  • Genuine engagement means listening to a customer’s needs before discussing a product and following up on what you learn to build lasting relationships 

  • Product value is best communicated by linking it to the customer's specific needs while providing balanced, accurate safety information
